title: Lake at rest with an emerged bump (SWASHES)
description: Still water at level 0.1 m over the 0.2 m bump, whose top stands out of the water between x = 8.59 and 11.41 m. Nothing should move: the depth stays max(0.1 − z, 0) and the velocity zero. A scheme that does not balance the bed slope against the pressure gradient, or mishandles the dry shoreline on a slope, sets the lake in motion.

citations.title: SWASHES: a compilation of shallow water analytic solutions for hydraulic and environmental studies
Proceedings of the 2nd workshop on dam-break wave simulation (EDF HE-43/97/016/B)

criteria.rationale: Nothing may move: worst velocity under 1 mm/s after 100 s. A scheme that does not balance the bed slope against the pressure gradient, or leaks at the dry shoreline on the bump, sets up currents of centimetres per second.
Average depth change under 0.5 mm: the lake must keep its water where it was.

Informational: the worst depth difference sits in the cells cut by the shoreline, where a cell-mean depth over a sloping bed differs from the exact depth at the cell centre by up to a few millimetres on these grids even when nothing moves.

convergence.not_applicable: The exact state is the initial state; a well-balanced scheme keeps it to rounding error on any grid, so there is no error to converge.
